# Education in Norway
Education in Norway is organized into three main levels: elementary (barneskole, ages 6–12), lower secondary (ungdomsskole, ages 13–16), and upper secondary school (videregående skole, ages 16–19). Compulsory education lasts for 10 years, covering the first two levels (grunnskole), with upper secondary optional but attended by the majority. Primary education focuses on foundational skills and introduces core subjects such as mathematics, English, science, religion (covering multiple faiths), geography, history, and social studies. Grading begins in lower secondary school, where students select electives and languages. Upper secondary offers both general and vocational paths, with reforms enabling flexibility between tracks and standardizing eligibility for higher education.
Higher education is provided mainly by public universities and university colleges, offering bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD programs, with admissions often determined by upper secondary grades and additional requirements for specialized fields. Most institutions are state-run, and private education is limited and heavily regulated. Special education is integrated within mainstream schools, emphasizing inclusive practices. Educators are required to hold relevant degrees and pedagogical qualifications, with different titles according to their training level (preschool teacher, adjunct, lecturer). The academic year runs from mid-August to mid-June, with long summer, Christmas, fall, and winter breaks.
Norway’s education system is characterized by universal access, broad state support, and a commitment to equity. Private schools and higher education institutions must meet stringent approval criteria and cannot select students subjectively. Special education and psychological services ensure support for pupils with learning differences. The grading system uses a six-point scale at lower levels and letter grades (Bologna system) at university level. Graduation from upper secondary school (videregående skole) and completion of required subjects qualifies students for higher education, with quality assured by national agencies.
